name: Jehangir Nusli Wadia
current_role: Non-executive promoter director, Bombay Burmah Trading Corp. and Britannia Industries (rejoined Wadia Group boards Nov 2024; reported to be returning as MD of Bombay Dyeing)
profile: Jeh Wadia (b. 1973), younger son of Nusli Wadia, ran Wadia Group airline GoAir/Go First from its 2005 launch until 2021 and was MD of Bombay Dyeing, where he founded Bombay Realty in 2011. He left the group's boards in 2021 and moved to London; Go First ceased flying in 2023. He returned to the group in late 2024 in non-executive board roles.
interesting_fact: He is a great-grandson of Pakistan's founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah, and was named a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Secretary of the Deendayal Research Institute under social reformer Nanaji Deshmukh; DRI adopted 500 villages in Chitrakoot to make them self-reliant. He also attended Millfield school in England and holds an MSc from Warwick.
notes: Go First's 2023 insolvency is a sensitive topic. No personal social accounts found. Best route is via Wadia Group company secretariat (Bombay Dyeing / Bombay Burmah). Not confirmed whether the Bombay Dyeing MD role has formally taken effect.

name: Omprakash Inani
current_role: Chairman, Shilpa Medicare Ltd (Raichur, Karnataka); Managing Director, Inok Cottons Pvt Ltd
profile: Omprakash Tulsiram Inani is chairman and a promoter-shareholder of Shilpa Medicare, a Raichur-based maker of oncology APIs, formulations, biologics and CDMO services co-founded with MD Vishnukant Bhutada. With 35+ years in business, he oversees the company's plants and also runs a cotton business, Inok Cottons, in Raichur.
interesting_fact: Shilpa Medicare grew from Raichur, a cotton town in northern Karnataka, into one of India's leading suppliers of oncology active pharmaceutical ingredients; Inani still runs a cotton ginning business alongside it.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond pharma he is a Managing Committee member of the Karnataka State Cotton Association (Hubli), a council member of Raichur's Taranath Shikshana Samsthe (which runs a medical/dental/pharmacy academy), and a trustee of the Akhil Bhartiya Maheshwari Education Trust in Pune.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts or interviews found. Company website lists no press/IR email; route via company enquiry form or company secretary listed in BSE/NSE filings.

name: Kevin J Jacobs
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, Hilton Worldwide; Director, Omega Healthcare Investors
profile: Kevin Jacobs (Cornell Hotel School '94) joined Hilton in 2008 as SVP corporate strategy, became treasurer, chief of staff and, in 2013, CFO, steering finances through Hilton's 2013 IPO era and asset-light shift. From 2020 to 2025 he also ran global development. Earlier he was at Fairmont Raffles, Host Hotels, PwC and Cushman & Wakefield; his wealth comes from Hilton equity compensation.
interesting_fact: He has spent essentially his whole career in hotel finance, from hospitality valuation at Cushman & Wakefield to running development for one of the world's largest hotel pipelines as Hilton's President, Global Development (2020-2025). He is a past chair of the American Hotel & Lodging Association.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the board of Goodwill of Greater Washington and is a trustee and executive committee member of the Federal City Council in Washington, D.C.
notes: Corporate executive (not a founder); wealth from Hilton stock. Regular presence on earnings calls and investor conferences; data-center/energy angle is weak, but hotel development/real-estate finance is a fit. Route via Hilton corporate communications.

name: Ashok Kumar Nedurumalli
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Vice Chairman, TeamLease Services (MD & CEO until Suparna Mitra took over effective Feb 2, 2026)
profile: Ashok Kumar Reddy Nedurumalli (SRCC, IIM Bangalore) co-founded India Life, a payroll and pension administration firm, with Manish Sabharwal and Mohit Gupta; Hewitt bought it in 2002. The pair then founded TeamLease, now one of India's largest staffing companies, listed in 2016. After about a decade as MD, he moved to Executive Vice Chairman in 2026.
interesting_fact: Before TeamLease, he and SRCC classmate Manish Sabharwal built India Life, a payroll and pension administration company that worked with 450-500 corporates within three years and was bought by Hewitt Associates in 2002. Its exit money went into TeamLease.
deep_cut_fact: Reddy and Sabharwal have been friends since their 1990 batch at Shri Ram College of Commerce. On why they started again after selling India Life, Reddy said: 'We still wanted to rule over our own kingdoms.'
notes: Publicly known as Ashok Reddy. He writes occasional columns for People Matters (https://www.peoplematters.in/author/ashok-reddy) and comments on India's jobs and labour market, which could make a good podcast angle. Beware namesakes (Digital.ai/Broadcom exec).

name: Kathleen M. Zimmermann
current_role: Director, Schneider National, Inc. (NYSE: SNDR); real estate investor
profile: Kathleen Zimmermann is a member of the Schneider family that controls Green Bay, Wisconsin trucking and logistics company Schneider National, founded by her grandfather Al Schneider in 1935. She has sat on Schneider's board since 2017 (with a break) and is a co-trustee of family trusts holding Class B shares, and is reported as a 10% owner. She now works as a real estate investor.
interesting_fact: Before joining the board she built a career in telecom sales leadership at Schneider Communications, Frontier Communications and Global Crossing, rather than in the family trucking business.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a bachelor's degree in marketing from Marquette University and is a licensed real estate agent who invests in property.
notes: Private family-member director with no public media presence. The grandfather/founder link comes from general Schneider history; the proxy confirms she is the sister of director Mary DePrey and a Schneider family member. The only realistic route is Schneider corporate communications.

name: W Randall Fowler
current_role: Co-CEO and director, Enterprise Products Partners (Houston); becomes sole CEO when Jim Teague retires on Jan 4, 2027
profile: Randy Fowler joined midstream giant Enterprise Products Partners in 1999, soon after its IPO. He was CFO in 2007-2015 and again in 2018-2024 and has been co-CEO since 2020. He has 48 years in energy finance and accounting, and his wealth is mainly Enterprise units. Under the July 2026 succession plan he takes sole command of the ~$120bn-enterprise-value pipeline, NGL and export business in January 2027.
interesting_fact: He is about to become sole CEO of one of the largest US energy infrastructure companies (pipelines, NGL fractionation, Gulf Coast export terminals). Chairman Randa Duncan credits outgoing co-CEO Teague with growing enterprise value from $1.8bn to almost $120bn over the period Fowler was there.
deep_cut_fact: A Louisiana Tech graduate (BS Accounting '78, MBA Finance), he was named the College of Business Distinguished Alumnus in 2012 and sits on its advisory board. He has also chaired the National Association of Publicly Traded Partnerships, the MLP industry group.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast: natural gas/NGL infrastructure and power demand from data centers are live topics for Enterprise. No personal social accounts. Route via Enterprise investor relations or media relations (named in quarterly press releases). Sources disagree on his MBA year ('89 vs '91).

name: Robert Lawrence Seelig
current_role: Executive Vice President & General Counsel (also handles Investor Relations), White Mountains Insurance Group
profile: Rob Seelig joined Bermuda-domiciled, Hanover NH-based insurance holding company White Mountains in 2002 from law firm Cravath, Swaine & Moore. He is its EVP and General Counsel and also its investor-relations contact. His wealth comes from long-tenured equity compensation at a company whose shares trade above $1,500.
interesting_fact: He doubles as White Mountains' general counsel and its investor-relations voice, unusual for a large-cap insurer, and is the named contact on the company's earnings releases.
deep_cut_fact: He holds three degrees from different schools: an undergraduate degree from Duke, an MBA from Duke's Fuqua School of Business, and a law degree from the University of Chicago Law School. He practised at Cravath before going in-house in 2002.
notes: As IR lead he is directly reachable through White Mountains' investor-relations channel (named on earnings releases with an office phone). The email on the bio page is obfuscated and was not reconstructed. He is a lawyer/executive rather than an entrepreneur, so the podcast fit is weak.

name: Nicholas Dominic Cortezi
current_role: Director and Executive Committee member, Ryan Specialty Holdings (NYSE: RYAN)
profile: Nick Cortezi joined Baltimore wholesale insurance broker All Risks, Ltd. in 1987, became CEO in 1999, and grew it from about $1.7m to roughly $250m in revenue, making it the fourth-largest US wholesale broker. He sold it to Ryan Specialty in 2020 and has been on Ryan's board since 2021. He also sits on boards including Datacubed Health, Cintana Education and Vennpoint Real Estate.
interesting_fact: At the 2020 merger, All Risks was on track to place $2.6bn in premiums with 850+ staff across 27 locations, which he built from a small Baltimore brokerage.
deep_cut_fact: Trained in foreign policy rather than insurance: he earned a diploma at Johns Hopkins SAIS in Bologna (1987), a BA in International Relations from Johns Hopkins (1988), and later a Master's in International Public Policy from SAIS DC (2008). He is a Life Member of the Council on Foreign Relations and a member of Business Executives for National Security.
notes: Also a board observer at Accrete AI, a possible AI/data angle. Low public-media profile. He was President of the National Association of Professional Surplus Lines Offices in 2002-03.

name: Roberto R Herencia
current_role: Executive Chairman & CEO, Byline Bancorp (Chicago); Chairman, First BanCorp / FirstBank Puerto Rico; Director, Banner Corp
profile: Banker Roberto Herencia spent 17 years at Popular Inc., including as president of Banco Popular North America, then ran Midwest Banc Holdings. In 2010 he founded community-bank investment fund BXM Holdings, which recapitalized Chicago's Metropolitan Bank Group and turned it into Byline Bank (IPO 2017). He has chaired Byline since 2013, has been CEO since 2021, and has chaired First BanCorp since 2011.
interesting_fact: He led a turnaround-by-recapitalization: through BXM Holdings he rebuilt failing Metropolitan Bank Group into Byline Bank, now a top Chicago commercial and SBA lender. At the same time he chaired First BanCorp through Puerto Rico's debt crisis.
deep_cut_fact: President Obama appointed him to the board of the Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC), the US government's development finance agency, in 2011. He holds a Georgetown finance degree and a Kellogg MBA.

public_contacts.value: brennie@bylinebank.com (Brooks O. Rennie, Head of Investor Relations, Investors/Media)

notes: Byline's IR head doubles as its media contact. The bank-turnaround story could fit an entrepreneurship angle.

name: Jonathan G. Weiss
current_role: Retired (June 1, 2025) as Co-CEO of Corporate & Investment Banking, Wells Fargo; no new public role found
profile: Jon Weiss spent about two decades at Wells Fargo. He joined its investment bank in 2005, co-headed investment banking and capital markets from 2008, led Wells Fargo Securities from 2014 and ran Wealth & Investment Management from 2017. From early 2020 he ran Corporate & Investment Banking, where net income rose about 40%. He retired in 2025; his wealth comes from Wells Fargo equity compensation.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership of Wells Fargo's Corporate & Investment Banking from early 2020, the unit's net income rose about 40% and revenue about 35%, according to CEO Charlie Scharf at his retirement.
notes: Retired from Wells Fargo in mid-2025, so Wells Fargo channels no longer represent him. No personal website or verified social accounts found. Watch for new board or private-equity roles. Common name; identity matched via SEC insider filings (Sr. EVP, WFC).

name: Michael T Fries
current_role: President & CEO (and Vice Chairman), Liberty Global; Executive Chairman, Liberty Latin America; director of Grupo Televisa and Lionsgate/Starz
profile: Mike Fries began as an investment banker and in 1990 became the fifth employee of United International Holdings, John Malone-backed cable venture that became UnitedGlobalCom and then Liberty Global, which he has run since 2005. He built it into Europe's largest cable/broadband operator (Virgin Media O2, VodafoneZiggo, Telenet). He is now breaking it up via spin-offs: Sunrise in 2024 and a planned Ziggo Group separation in 2027.
interesting_fact: He is the son of Charles Fries, the Hollywood producer dubbed the 'Godfather of the television movie', and one of eight children. His first real job was in his father's office. He is also the lead singer of The Moderators, a classic-rock cover band of Colorado executives that has raised millions for charity.
deep_cut_fact: As a kid in Southern California he delivered newspapers from his bicycle, and he says running a global cable company is basically the same job at scale. Denver's DSST Public Schools named him its 'Slice of Pi' honoree in 2016. He is also an adventure skier who has gone heli-skiing in British Columbia with his management team.
notes: Highly media-accessible, with frequent CNBC and conference appearances. Liberty Global co-owns edge data-center operator AtlasEdge (a JV with DigitalBridge) and is a major European fibre/broadband player, a good fit for data-center and infrastructure topics. Based in Denver.

name: Ryan J. Watts
current_role: Co-founder, President & CEO, Denali Therapeutics (South San Francisco)
profile: Ryan Watts (BS Utah '00, PhD Stanford '04) spent 11 years at Genentech, where he started its Alzheimer's drug-discovery effort and led neuroscience research. In 2015 he co-founded Denali Therapeutics to develop drugs for neurodegenerative disease. Its TransportVehicle platform carries large-molecule drugs across the blood-brain barrier, and its first product, an enzyme therapy for Hunter syndrome, moved to approval and launch in 2025-26.
interesting_fact: Denali's core bet is engineering biologics to cross the blood-brain barrier, a long-standing obstacle in CNS drug development, using its TransportVehicle platform. Watts has run the company as CEO since August 2015 and argenx co-founder Tim Van Hauwermeiren joined its board in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A Cottonwood High School (Utah) graduate, as an undergraduate at the University of Utah he was a teaching assistant for cone-snail-venom pioneer Baldomero 'Toto' Olivera and worked as a pediatric surgical technician at Primary Children's Medical Center.
notes: Scientist-founder who talks openly about biotech building. The IR contact named in April 2026 releases is nielsen@dnli.com. The energy/data-center fit is weak, but the founder story is strong.

name: Russell Stokes
current_role: Retired from GE Aerospace (July 2026) after leading Commercial Engines & Services; independent director, UPS
profile: Russell Stokes spent about 29 years at GE. He ran GE Transportation, then GE Energy Connections, and became president and CEO of GE Power in 2017 during its restructuring. He later ran GE Aviation Services and, from 2022, GE Aerospace's $27bn Commercial Engines & Services unit with about 12,000 people. Mohamed Ali succeeded him in January 2026, and he advised CEO Larry Culp until retiring in July 2026.
interesting_fact: He ran GE Power, GE's gas-turbine and power-plant business, through its 2017-2019 turnaround and then helped lead GE Aerospace's commercial engine business. That background spans both energy generation and jet engines, highly relevant to the gas-turbine supply crunch driven by data-center power demand.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in sales at a PC manufacturer before joining GE's Financial Management Program, and holds a finance degree from Cleveland State University. In Atlanta he served on the board of Usher's New Look, the youth-leadership nonprofit founded by the singer Usher, and on Junior Achievement of Atlanta's executive committee.
notes: Retired from GE in July 2026 (Jan 15, 2026 GE 8-K/press release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/40545/000004054526000002/exhibit991pressrelease11526.htm), so GE channels no longer apply. Still a UPS director and a Morehouse School of Medicine trustee. No verified personal social accounts found. Strong guest fit for energy/power-equipment topics; reach via his board affiliations.
